blog_title: JEE Mains 2021 April Strategy | Best Book for JEE Advanced 2021
description: Now that we are past the March attempt of IIT JEE Mains 2021, our strategies must focus on the April attempt of IIT JEE Mains 2021. This is a crucial time as a lot of IIT JEE aspirants are confused whether they should start preparing for JEE Advanced or should they focus on JEE Mains April. So here is Margdarshan trying to clear the clutter inside your minds and help you take the right path.    Let’s Analyse The JEE Mains March Paper    First things first, the March attempt paper was relatively tougher compared to the February attempt. That was expected, however, and we can safely assume that the coming attempts could be even tougher. In the March attempt, the Maths section was especially high on difficulty, while the Chemistry section consisted of tricky questions. It must be noticed though that a lot of chemistry questions were directly NCERT based, especially in the Organic and Inorganic Chemistry section.   Before We Dive Into The Strategy   One must evaluate where they stand after the March attempt before they begin further preparation. Once the answers are tallied with any answer key from a credible source, one can get a fair idea of where they stand in terms of the expected score. That understanding is crucial in strategizing further preparation for JEE 2021.   For Expected March JEE Mains Score Below 120   If one is expecting a March JEE Mains score of 120 or below, they can expect to secure a rank of somewhere between 15,000 and 20,000. Sure, there will be a few NITs and other good colleges that will be available to candidates with such a rank, but they will have to compromise with their branch. On the other hand, if they have strong branch preferences, they will have to compromise with the institute. Thus, it is suggested for these candidates that instead of going for JEE Advanced preparation, they must focus on giving the April attempt and scoring better. During this period they must focus on the following:    Thorough NCERT revision Solving PYQs Giving Mock Tests Periodically and Analyzing      For Expected March JEE Mains Score Between 120 & 150   For the expected March JEE Mains score between 120 and 150, the rank could lie somewhere between 7,000 and 15,000. At this rank, one could easily get NITs along with getting their preferred branches, as well as a few IITs too with middling branches. However, getting the Top branches at preferred IITs would be difficult. Thus, this category of students must strike a balance between preparing for JEE Mains April Attempt as well as JEE Advanced 2021. These students must focus on the following:    Mock Tests, focusing on accuracy Solving PYQs Revise Short Notes    For Expected March JEE Mains Score Above 150   Needless to say, the candidates with a score of 150+ must focus heavily on JEE Advanced preparation, while keeping a slight eye on JEE Mains April Attempt too. For these candidates, Margdarshan would like to suggest a few books to help them in their JEE Advanced Preparation. These books include    Maths - Arihant or Cengage Physics - D.C. Pandey (Objective) Organic Chemistry - Himanshu Pandey, O.P.Tandon Inorganic Chemistry - NCERT, J.D.Lee Physical Chemistry - R.K.Mukherjee    Along with these, the candidates must focus on Mocks and PYQs as they will help in both JEE Mains and JEE Advanced preparation. Additionally, candidates with score above 170 should give PYQs as a Mock Test only, preferably on alternate days, and focus on analysis on the same.   We hope the above information helps aspirants choose the right strategy. One can feel free to contact Margdarshan on Social Media or our helpline to get further guidance. Margdarshan wishes all aspirants the Best of Luck !

blog_title: Preparation Strategies for Board Examination, Top 5 Strategies
description: While most of us are heavily focused on IIT JEE Mains or NEET preparation, one issue that a number of Competitive Exam aspirants frequently face is the constant dilemma of distribution of time and effort between JEE or NEET preparation and Board Exam preparation for class 12th. The major issue is that the majority of aspirants are not able to devise a clear and efficient strategy for board exam preparation, and therefore end up spending unnecessarily large amounts of time on it, thereby hampering their Competitive Exams preparation too.   At Margdarshan, we have come up with a set of 5 key pointers that, if followed, can help you strike the perfect balance, and will also ensure that you perform well in the Board exams too. Let's delve deep into this.   Proper and Planned Revisions   A big set of students usually complain post exams that even though they had studied certain topics, they weren’t able to fully justify that in the exam. The reason behind that is simple - lack of thorough revision. When you study a topic, it gets stored in your mind. Then, when you move on to the next topic and so forth, the memory of older ones begins to fade. Therefore, it becomes critical that before the exam, you do a thorough end to end revision of each topic. When you revise topics, your brain accesses old memory cells that got suppressed by the piling of more information, and therefore, the memory now becomes refreshed and there is a huge chance that you would be able to recall that topic in the exam.   Solve Previous Year Question Papers   One common thread in Board Exams across the country, whether it be State Board, CBSE or ICSE, is that a lot of questions from the previous years get repeated in the exam. As such, it helps to have gone through and solved the previous years’ question papers, especially for the last 10 years. Apart from the questions getting repeated, solving previous years question papers gives one an understanding of the pattern of question paper, the topical weightage, test taking practice and time management.   Planning Your Study Time Table   Board exams require conceptual knowledge as well as the ability to write descriptive answers. Therefore, the study needs to be elaborate and in depth, and the focus must be on being able to reproduce the whole concept in the exam. In such a scenario, your study plan must focus on detailed revision and detailed answer writing practice. One must plan their study time table in a way that high concept and high weightage topics get maximum coverage. Also, one must do a little research on best answer writing methods and get their answers checked by experts to ensure that they are up to the mark.   Will it help in Competitive Examination’s Preparation?   A lot of people treat Board Exams and Competitive Exams as separate entities. But the truth is, they are just two different pillars based on the same conceptual foundation. Essentially, every competitive exam is just a slightly more complex and application oriented test of the same concepts that one learns for board exams. Therefore, devoting time to Board exam preparation will only help you strengthen your base, which you can then build on for your competitive exams like JEE Mains, NEET, etc. Also, sometimes aspirants get stuck in competitive exams where they are unable to ascertain whether the methods and formulae they are applying are indeed applicable for the given question, and in such instances, having a sound base of clear concepts can come in handy.   We hope that the above pointers can help you prepare well for the Board exams without compromising on the Competitive Exam preparation. For any further help, feel free to reach out to Margdarshan, and we would be happy to help. All the Best!

description: JEE Advanced 2021 is ringing near and so is the student's anxiety. But, the COVID-19 may again be a decisive factor in rescheduling the exam and there are pretty good probability of the exam getting postponed. But to keep yourself ready for every circumstance, it would be a wise take to be advance in your preparations rather than focusing on the date of the exam. To make your JEE advanced preparation more viable and exam-specific, here we provide a tailored strategy for the students. JEE Advanced Strategy As far as an airtight strategy for cracking JEE advanced is concerned, there is no ‘one size fits all scheme. But, some universal techniques are helpful for all:  Set your daily, weekly and monthly targets:  Taking the announced JEE Advanced date to be final, you have less than 2 months left for the D Day. So, set yourself productive and achievable targets on a daily, weekly and monthly basis. Divide your whole syllabus accordingly so that you can go through every topic of the curriculum well before the exam.  Don’t start Cramming  It is a general tendency of students to hop on cramming the concepts when the exam approaches near. This is the biggest mistake to beware of. Turn to mock tests:  Almost all of the previous IIT qualifiers and specially toppers have briefed us on the significance of mock tests in getting you closer to success in the exam. Scrutinize your strong and weak areas, note them down and spare 2-3 hours from your routine to work on the weak zones.  Finalize your sectioning scheme  To be in rhythm during the exam, prepare your pattern to be followed during performing the exam ready in advance. Prepare robust sectioning based on your weak and strong subjects.  Be always in the learning zone  Apart from study hours, you can use your miscellaneous time in preparation for the exam as well. Paste formula notes at various places like your room door, bathroom, exercise area, etc. This will help you memorize important formulas during showers, exercises and normal passing bys.    Important Points The perfect warrior never compromise on any vertical. Subjective preparations are first requirement towards clearing your exam. Though the registration for the exam is not open yet, but once it opens complete your JEE Advanced registration on time to prevent last minute rush. Practice an hour of meditation and yoga to increase your productivity. Rely on healthy food to keep your health optimum. Try to stay away from negative news. Be in touch with friends and teachers to be updated regarding any developments.    Be ahead of the time and the race to mark up your name in your dream IIT. A perfect strategy and an earnest endeavor is all you need to call out successfully to the JEE advanced 2021.

blog_title: JEE Mains Counselling 2021 Procedure | Steps to fill JoSAA Counselling

And, we know your mind is hovered by many questions now about the procedure and process of counselling. So, here is everything you need to know about JEE Mains counselling 2021. JEE Mains Counselling 2021 The complete process of JEE Mains counselling 2021 is undertaken by Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA). This year also, they will be scheduling it once the results are out. The counselling would be held through online mode. After JoSAA counselling, the leftover vacant seats will further be administered by Central Seat Allocation Board(CSAB) Steps in the Counselling   Registration- The students qualifying for the JEE Mains can participate in the counselling To initiate the process, the candidate needs to have to make online registration at the official website of JoSAA 2021. You have to use your JEE Mains 2021 roll number and password for logging in. All the fields must be filled accurately and after that, click the confirmation button. Choice Filling – Upon registration, the candidate needs to fill in preferred choices of institutions and courses they want admission in. It’s suggested to fill maximum choices for a maximum probability of getting admission. Once you fill in the choices, lock them or they will be automatically locked once the choice filling is closed. Mock Seat Allotment- Before provisional seat allocation, the JoSAA will conduct two rounds of mock counselling to make the process more comprehensive to the students. It will provide a better image to students of the probable institute they can get admitted to based on their scores. Analyzing the mock seat allotment results, candidate can change the choices. After the choice filling is closed, 6 rounds of subsequent provisional counselling will be held. Provisional Seat Allotment And Acceptance- Based on your scores, choices and cut-off marks, you will be allotted a seat at an institution from your preference list. To accept the seat, the candidate needs to make the fee payment through E-Challan or SBI net banking. Do keep the E-Challan receipt for further references. Candidates must also download the provisional seat allotment letter.  Once the candidate accepts the seat, he will be asked to choose from 3 options viz:  Freeze- You lock the institute you got admission at and do not want to participate in further rounds of counselling. Float- You lock the institute you got admission at, but want to participate in further rounds of counselling to know about more options. Slide- You are open to joining higher courses if available in the same institute you got admission to.  After the seat acceptance payment, the candidate needs to report to the assigned institute for document verification. Document Verification  Further developments in your admission include documents verification at the institute you get admission to. Following are the essential documents you need to carry for the verification:  Provisional Seat Allotment Letter issued by official JoSAA portal. E-Challan receipt as proof of online seat acceptance payment. A valid identity card(government-issued) 3 passport size photos similar to the one uploaded during candidate registration. JEE Mains Admit Card JEE Mains 2021 scorecard 12th class official mark-sheet Date of Birth proof Category card if applicable Disability documents if applicable.  How Can We Help? blog_title: CBSE Class 12th Marking Scheme| CBSE Latest News on Marking Scheme
description: After the historic take of C.B.S.E on the 1st of June 2021 on cancelling class 12th board exams, the students were all inquisitive about how they are going to be evaluated now and when would C.B.S.E class 12 result will be declared. The wait is over, as the 12-member committee set by the Education Ministry to develop robust and fair criteria of evaluation has finally come out with their 12th class marking scheme. The attorney general presented the scheme in front of the Supreme Court on 17th June 2021. After listening to the attorney general, the supreme court declared to pass the final orders on the same on 21st June 2021. Now you all must be on the edges of your seats to know exactly what’s in the marking scheme. So, here is a detailed explanation of the scheme proposed by the committee for the Class 12th evaluation. Highlights of the new scheme  According to the scheme, class 12th result will be developed from the performance of students in class 10th, 11th and 12th by far. The committee referenced a ratio of 30:30:40 for class 10th, 11th and 12th contribution to the result. The only theory part of the exam will be evaluated by these criteria.   30% proportion will be from the average of best three subject's theory score in class 10th final exams. 30% proportion will be from class 11th final exams theory result. 40% proportion will be from class 12th unit/sessional/pre-board exams theory result.   Practical marks will be based on the 12th class only. The schools are guided to set a committee headed by the principal and two PGT teachers to determine the result for their school students. The result is said to be out by 31st July 2021 and Supreme Court has ordered the committee to come out with a strong grievance redressal pattern for the students. The students unsatisfied with the results will be given the option to appear for a physical exam after the COVID conditions become conducive.  Benefits The scheme is developed by reliable think tanks of the education ministry, so we cannot simply rule it out. Apart from helping avoid physical exams in these dreadful conditions, the scheme also has some more benefits:  Three academic years of a student will be considered for evaluation, the students who couldn’t perform well during a pandemic can be backed by their previous better results. The inclusion of theory scores only makes it more credible as knowledge is kept as the base of evaluation. The choice of appearing for the physical exam for students not contended with the result opens the door for normal evaluation as well.  Loopholes It is practically impossible to create a scheme that is foolproof and is acceptable to all. The C.B.S.E  class 12 marking scheme is also confronting criticism due to the following reasons:  Usually, some students, especially those preparing for engineering and medical entrances do not pay much attention to the scoring in class 11th. The scheme will thus degrade the potential score they could get through the normal pattern. The scheme seems unfair to students who worked really hard this year but doesn’t have a good scoring in class 10th and 11th. Evaluation by schools makes the process prone to alterations at various platforms. No concrete process is provided regarding rationalization or moderation of the scores. A robust strategy to redress the resentments is missing in the scheme.  What students should do now? The scheme is not yet finalized completely and is subjected to many changes. So students must not panic until the official results are out. Also, after the 12th class result declaration, the option of appearing for a physical exam after the pandemic conditions become facilitative is always open if you are not happy with the evaluation. So, students must keep their focus on their further preparations for various entrance exams. Conclusion The marking scheme for C.B.S.E 12 Class has launched another wave of uncertainty, worries, hopes and concerns. The only and best option is to patiently wait for things to get fully transparent and to trust the democratic powers residing in the nation. Meanwhile, stay tuned to Margdarshan for all necessary C.B.S.E latest updates.

blog_title: What is JEE Advanced Exam| How to get admission into IIT?
description: IITs in India are not just some regular technical institutes but brands in themselves. The highly dreamed corridors of these premium institutes have seen some of the best CEOs, writers, scientists, MDs, politicians, and almost all types of connoisseurs strolling their way as students there. Given to the potential of the IITs, each year lakhs of students dream to get a seat in one of them.  How to get admission to IIT? Everyone knows that the ride to IIT is quite demanding. The success rate in the whole procedure of getting into IIT is less than1%. But, where does it all begin? Many would say that it all begins with preparation, coaching, filling up the forms, etc. But, the real quest to get into an IIT begins with a knack. A knack for playing around Physics, Mathematics, and Chemistry. When you start looking at the world from a more scientific perspective that means you are ready for the steep journey to IIT.   After a good number of years' preparation(depends on when you realize about your knack and start preparing for getting admission into IIT after 12th), your practical trip to IIT pursues with following steps:  JEE Mains Registration  JEE Mains exam JEE Advanced registration JEE Advanced exam JoSAA Counseling   <iframe allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" frameborder="0" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/eAsjQ3R1iPQ" title="YouTube video player" width="560"></iframe> The students who qualified JEE advanced are able to fill all the IITs, NITs, GFTIs and IIITs in their choice filling during JoSAA Counseling. The students who qualified only JEE Mains can fill only NITs, GFTIs and IIITs in their choice filling as they are not eligible to apply for IITs. If you manage to get a good score and all India rank in JEE Advanced then with subsequent steps of document verification and admission formalities for the IIT allotted to you, your dream journey consumes at a seat in the IIT classroom only to start a new academic journey in finest educational ambiance What is JEE Advanced? The filtration process to get the most deserving candidates for placing in IITs goes through many steps and the most significant of them is JEE Advanced. JEE Advanced is the second stage exam after JEE Mains to get admission to IITs. The top rankers from JEE Mains are eligible for appearing in the JEE Advanced, qualifying which further opens the doors of IITs for them based on their ranking and score. So for your question to what is JEE advanced exam, the answer is that it is the gateway that you have to clear for getting into an IIT. Each year one of the Indian Institutes of Technology organizes the JEE advanced exam. History Before 2013, students used to appear for AIEEE for getting admission to NITs, GFTIs, and some other private technical institutes. For admission to IITs, the students had to appear for the IIT-JEE exam. All the students were allowed to sit in the IIT-JEE exam. But, from 2013 the AIEEE and IIT-JEE pattern was scrapped and JEE Mains and Advanced were installed. This step generated a screening process for admission to IIT before the actual exam,  that is JEE Advanced, as only limited qualifiers from JEE Mains are eligible for appearing in JEE Advanced. Exam pattern: mode, number of questions, type of questions, marking scheme, etc. JEE Advanced Exam pattern shows just minute changes each year and usually, it is the same every time. The changes are not major and won’t surprise you. It is always beneficial to thoroughly get acquainted with the exam pattern and important information like number and types of questions, marking scheme, etc. for the exam. The organizing IIT always issues a detailed brochure about the full pattern of the exam well in advance each year. For your convenience, here is detailed information about everything you need to know about the JEE Advanced:  No. Of Papers: The exam is conducted in two segments, Paper I and Paper-II. Both the papers are mandatory to appear by the candidates. Exam duration: 3 hours for each paper. Mode: JEE Advanced is conducted in online mode and is a computer-based exam. Types of Questions: The JEE Advanced question paper comprises of generally four types of questions- Multiple Choice Questions, Numerical Data Type Questions, Match the following type questions, and paragraph-based questions. You expect any of these types in your exam. Sections: The question paper consists of three sections, each for Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.  Marking Scheme: According to the JEE Advanced latest pattern there will be negative, partial, and zero marking:   Negative Marking- For MCQ-type questions with only one correct answer( -2 )marks will be given for a wrong answer.   For MCQ-type questions with multiple correct answers (-1), marks will be given if no correct option is chosen.  Partial Marking- For MCQ type questions with more than one correct answer +3 marks will be given for choosing 3 out of 4 correct options, +2 marks will be given for choosing 2 out of 3 or more correct options and +1 marks will be given for choosing only 1 out of 2 or more correct options. Zero marking- For all the unattempted questions and wrong numerical type questions 0 marks will be given.  To understand the pattern more deeply you can see previous year JEE Advanced question papers and mock test series by Margdarshan. JoSAA Counseling  Joint Seat Allocation Authority organizes counseling for admissions to IITs, NITs, IITs, and GFTIs based on JEE Mains and JEE Advanced scores. The counseling procedure begins after JEE mains exam is conducted for all the students. It starts with online registration and choice filling and six subsequent rounds of seat allotment are held.  JoSAA Counseling process can be confusing and time-consuming and since many of you would be gearing up for JEE Advanced preparation, Margdarshan we smoothly guide you through the JoSAA Counseling process. For more details on JoSAA counseling 2021, you can read this blog JEE Counselling 2021 Procedure | Steps to fill JoSAA Counselling About JEE advanced 2021 The JEE Advanced 2021 which will be organized by IIT Kharagpur, was supposed to be held on 3rd July 2021, but due to the pandemic's new wave, the exam was postponed. The exact JEE Advanced 2021 Exam date is still not out officially and students are still waiting for some concrete information. Other Information unique to JEE Advanced 2021 are:  JEE Advanced 2021 is special as students who qualified JEE Mains 2020 but couldn’t appear in JEE Advanced 2020 are also eligible to appear for JEE Advanced 2021. They do not have to qualify JEE Mains 2021 again. The students from JEE Mains 2020 will be considered in addition to the 2021 batch and thus there will be no loss to the new batch. The female quota seats which used to be 20% will not be the same this year. This time IITs will decide the number of female seats on their own. The restriction of a minimum 75% marks in the 12th board exams is lifted this time and students only need to pass the 12th board exam. 3 attempts are allowed to appear in the JEE Mains and JEE advanced exams now.  For JEE Advanced 2021 syllabus you can click on the given link. JEE Advanced Physics syllabus: Click Here JEE Advanced Chemistry syllabus: Click Here JEE Advanced Maths syllabus: Click Here JEE Advanced syllabus 2021 PDF Free Download: Click Here Conclusion If you are going to appear for JEE Mains 2021 or JEE Advanced 2021 then the countdown has already begun. So tighten up your laces for a sprint that you never did before. Immerse yourself in the endeavors that can make your dream to sit in an IIT come true. For more information and important updates about JEE Mains 2021 and JEE Advanced 2021 stay tuned to Margdarshan

blog_title: CBSE Latest News 2021 for Class 12 and Class 10| Impact on NEET and JEE
description: When all are busy and curious about the JEE Mains 2021, NEET 2021, and C.B.S.E class 12th board exams 2022 evaluation criteria, an important thing that was being ignored was, ‘What about 10th and 12th board exams of session 2021-22?’. The students were totally confused about how they will be evaluated for these crucial academic years. But, the latest news about C.B.S.E class 10th and 12th is that the board has issued the evaluation criteria for the students in the 10th and 12th of the academic year 2021-22 well in time. On 5th July 2021, C.B.S.E released a special assessment scheme for the current 10th and 12th class batches of the 2021-22 academic session. The new pattern signals toward two terms of board exam nation scheduled to be held in November-December 2021 and March- April  2022. Here is everything you need to know about the new scheme: Board Exams Will Be Geld In Two Terms The key announcement made by the Central Board is that the present 10th and 12th classes will be divided into two terms Term I and Term II. Both the terms will cover 50% syllabus each and will be concluded with a Term board exam. Here are some highlights of the announcement:  Each term will cover 50% of the syllabus. A board exam based on the assigned 50% syllabus will be conducted after each term. The Term I board exams will be held in November-December 2021. The schedule is flexible and there is a window period of 4-8 weeks for exam conduction for all parts of the country. The Term II Board exams will be held in April-March 2022. The term I exams will be a 90 minutes MCQ-based exam on an OMR sheet. Questions will be case-based assertion-reasoning type. description: All the four sessions of JEE Mains 2021 are over and results for three sessions are already out. Now in between JEE Mains and JEE Advanced lies a very significant aspect, the scores. To establish the eligibility for JEE Advanced aspirants JEE Mains 2021 score must lie between the set percentile range. With the word ‘Percentile' here comes the topic of this blog, which is JEE Mains 2021 marks V/s percentile.  Students are always baffled about the conversion of raw scores into percentile and how they are going to be evaluated based on the percentile for JEE Advanced and NIT Admissions. So, here we are with detailed information about the relationship between JEE Mains 2021 marks and percentile.  What is percentile and why is it necessary?  Now a very common and obvious question that might trigger your nervous system is that why to introduce a new parameter when we already have fair scores. Let us clear the air about that. JEE Mains is conducted in four sessions and despite all efforts, it is practically not possible to keep the difficulty levels of all the sessions to be equal. So to prevent any discrepancy in results and to provide a fair chance to all the aspirants, the normalization technique is used. Under this, the raw scores are converted into percentile based on a foolproof and well-studied formula taking the average raw scores of each session into account. In this way, students of equal caliber are placed into the equal percentile range to prevent any biases in the results.    How does NTA convert raw score to percentile? National Testing Agency uses a unique formula of Normalisation on how to convert raw score to percentile. The highest scores of each section are put under the same percentile and accordingly, the lower marks are turned into comparative percentiles. In this way, the students with the same potential are kept under the same percentile for a fair selection.   In case of ties:  The percentile score is calculated to seven decimal places to prevent the chances of ties, but, in case if there are students with the same percentile then the following criteria is followed :    A student with a higher rank in mathematics will get a higher rank.  For the same percentile and equal mathematics score students with a higher score in Physics will be ranked higher.  For equal percentile and equal marks in mathematics and physics students with a higher score in chemistry will be ranked higher.  For equal percentile and equal marks in all three subjects, student with less negative responses will be ranked higher.  If the tie remains then the older candidate will be ranked higher.  Aspirants who appeared for more than one session will be evaluated based on the best of all attempts score. Marks V/s percentile   JEE Marks and Percentile are associated based on guidelines developed by NTA after diligent consideration of keeping the process fair for all. The below table depicts Marks VS Percentile in JEE Mains 2021 based on the difficulty level of your exam. You can know your expected percentile based on your raw score with this. Your JEE Main marks and rank will decide your future in JOSAA counseling 2021 and JEE Advanced eligibility. The following table will help you to know about your next steps. It is a more comprehensive list as it is developed considering the difficulty factor of all the sessions. blog_title: CSAB 2021 Dates(out), Registration procedure, Documents, Seat allotment procedure
description: CSAB used to conduct counselling for NIT, IIIT and GFTI but they were not included in JOSAA counselling. Now CSAB only conducts counselling for a special round which is conducted after the completion of 6 rounds of JOSAA . This round is for vacant seats. The Central Seat Allocation Board has released the CSAB 2021 schedule online. The CSAB 2021 schedule for the special round of seat allocation has been released at csab.nic.in. Interested candidates can participate in the special CSAB 2021 seat allotment by visiting the official website and registering for the seat allotment process. The CSAB 2021 registration window will be open from 28th to 30th November 2021 after the display of vacant seats after JoSAA counseling 2020 on 18th November 2021. Moreover, the seats left vacant after all the round of JoSAA 2021 will be displayed by the authorities on 18 November 2021. Further, registration, payment of participation and choice filling will start on 28th November 2021.  The Round 1 of Display of Seat Allotment Result will be on 2 nd Dec 2021 (Thu) (17:00 hrs) The last day for responding to query for Special Round 1 will be on 5 th Dec 2021 (Sun) Till 14:00 hrs The Special Round 2 of Display of Seat Allotment Result will happen on 7 th Dec 2021 (Tue). The reporting at the allotted institute, both in-person and online will begin on 7 th Dec 2021 (Tue) (12:00 hrs) To 9 th Dec 2021 (Thu) (12:00 hrs)  Central Seat Allocation Board will hold the counselling for admission through three channels – CSAB NEUT, Supernumerary, special rounds. Moreover, the registration procedure for CSAB NEUT has already begun from 9th November 2021.  Also read JEE Mains 2022 Preparation Strategy, Free Mock Test- Click Here  CSAB 2021 Special Round Schedule The Central Seat Allocation Board has announced the schedule for the CSAB Special Counselling Round for candidates who have attempted JEE Mains or JEE Advanced Exams. The schedule is as mentioned below, but the dates are subject to changes based on the circumstances at that given point in time.     Counseling Event   Dates     Display of vacancies after JoSAA Counselling Session   27th Nov 2021 (Sat)    Registration, Payment of Processing Fee, Choice Filling - Start Date   28th Nov 2021 (Sun)    Registration, Payment of Processing Fee, Choice Filling - End Date   30th Nov 2021 (Tue)    Display of Seat Allotment - Round 1   2nd Dec 2021 (Thu)       CSAB Special Round 2021 Eligibility All candidates who were eligible for JoSAA as per JEE Main 2021 Ranks will be eligible to participate in the CSAB special round as per the following eligibility norms:    Candidates who have not registered in JoSAA till now but are eligible based on JEE Main 2021 ranks, will be eligible for participating in the CSAB special rounds for NITs/IIITs/ other GFTIs (except IITs) as per JoSAA 2021 / CSAB 2021 rules. Those who participated in JoSAA and were allotted seats will also be eligible for participating in the Special Rounds for NITs/IIITs/ other GFTIs (except IITs). Those who participated in JoSAA but did not get any seat will also be eligible for participating in the Special Rounds for NITs/IIITs/ other GFTIs (except IITs). Candidates who participated in JoSAA and got a seat in an IIT will also be eligible for participating in the Special Rounds for NITs/IIITs/ other GFTIs (except IITs)  If a candidate fails to register for the special rounds from November 28 to 30, 2021, he/she will not be entertained for seat allotment. Candidates, who have opted“ Not to participate in the special round” at the time of reporting at the allotted institute, cannot register in CSAB special round. blog_title: New Year Resolution of JEE Aspirants| Preparation Resolution for JEE Aspirants 2022
description: 2021 is ending paving the way for 2022 and just like 2020, 2021 also had a pretty good proportion devoted to the jinx of COVID. Now apart from all the traditional hopes from the new year, we are also hoping to get a permanent break from the on-off cynical scenarios of the pandemic. Talking of traditions, the annual routine of new year resolutions is on its seasonal peak and we being your companion to success are yet again present for you with this burning topic of new year resolutions. Being a student, your life is very demanding for some strict and serious actions and if you are a JEE aspirant then the demands increase exponentially. So, to get the maximum out of your routine in your new annual chapter here are some new year resolutions for JEE Aspirants.  Wait! I know you are very much excited to know what your resolution should be but let me interrupt your excitement with a reality check. Here are some pointers. Get a pen and a paper and be honest in answering to every pointer.  Did you make a resolution last year?  If yes, jump to the next pointer If no, jump to pointer 3  Did you manage to stick to it for more than 6 months?  If yes, jump to the conclusion If no, jump to the next pointer  Are you stalwart on following your resolution wholeheartedly this year?  In either case, jump to the conclusion. Conclusion Structuring up a resolution is a fragile move if you lack a strong determination and a strict demeanor to follow it effectively. It is very easy to announce a resolution on new year's eve’s party with your friends but it becomes more difficult to follow it from the very next day when your sleep-stricken eyes ditch your alarm clock. So, if you are ready to battle with your procrastinating and lazy side then only continue with this article. Merely reading the resolutions and picking your personal favorite is just a joke to yourself.  If you feel that you are ready to embrace the true motive of resolving for the new year then here are some great and helpful resolutions to add to your productivity and catalyze your JEE preparation speed.   I resolve this year that I will maintain my health in its pink.  There is no valuable wealth than health as if you are not healthy then you won’t be able to put in desired efforts in your studies as well. So, one of the foremost new year resolutions for JEE aspirants must be to keep themselves healthy. Avoid junk food, drink an ample amount of water, eat a balanced diet, do yoga and exercise daily, and set up a healthy routine for yourself this year, and enjoy the outputs in your academic productivity.  I resolve that I will minimize my screen time this year.  The biggest pitfall in the passage of JEE preparation is the distracting elements like social media, OTT channels, and the constant ding-dong of your smartphone notifications. We all know that once you start scrolling your mobile then minutes turn into hours rapidly and at the end of the day you realize that the whole day went in vain. Stop using social media, watching series and movies, and wasting time online as these habits can wait but JEE won’t.  I resolve that I will learn something new almost daily this year.  Student years are a golden time to learn and the maximum you learn in these years will show up in your personality in the future. Start reading good books, join online courses of your interested niche, learn new and advanced topics of JEE, or polish your skills. The keyword is LEARN DAILY! Don’t let any day go to waste and enrich your portfolio each day with new skills, knowledge, and information.  I resolve that I will increase my study hours this year.  You yourself don’t know your true potential and if you push yourself a bit more then you might get surprised with your new outputs. This year resolve to increase your study hours if you feel that you can snatch more time for studies from your routine.   I resolve that I will do at least one mock test series daily this year  We know that we have told you the benefits of doing mock tests umpteen times but we can’t help as they are worth it. So, if you are still lacking mock practice then resolve to do at least one mock test series daily. It will boost your JEE preparation vividly. For most realistic and exam oriented test series you can practice the free mock test series provided by Margdarshan. Our test series are smartly designed by subject experts. Your resolution depends on your current routine and these are just a help. Our main motive is to encourage you to bring positive and efficient changes in your life taking the excuse of the new year. Important Points If you are ready with your resolution then please keep the following points in your mind to get maximum out of your determination: Be practical The biggest reason behind failure in your resolution is setting up a target that is not achievable practically. So, aim for the routine and habits that are practical to follow.  Be Mature Don’t follow a routine or resolution just to boast about it. Be honest to yourself as you are not a kid anymore. Be mature and resolve for outputs, not praises. Be diligent  After a week, fortnight, or a month your energy and enthusiasm will start waning. This is the time when you are most intent to drop the resolution and give in to your laziness. Show your tenacity at that point to sustain to your words. Add resolutions-  It is not written in any constitution or any holy book that you have to wait for the new year for sticking to some good habit. So when you become habitual to previous resolutions, add some more to your routine. It is never bad to be good after all. Take breaks  It is always good to take breaks from your routine to prevent monotony. Take monthly breaks from your routine and get a cheat day for recreational activities. Enjoy the break to the fullest and resume your routine afterward with more energy. Celebrate your success Treat yourself with your favorite meal or anything you like quarterly or in two months to celebrate the success of your resolution. This way you would be more motivated to follow your new year resolution.  Margdarshan wishes you a very happy and prosperous New Year and we hope that this year proves to be a positive turning poi t in your career.

blog_title: WHAT TO EXPECT AFTER GETTING INTO MEDICAL SCHOOL? | NEET UG RESULT 2022
description: NEET UG 2022 result will soon be declared, and you will get busy with the admission process. We know the process is a bit stressful but believe us, it’s rewarding. You must be confused as to what to expect from a medical school. We are here to help you with that. MBBS in India is a 5.5-year-long degree including a one-year mandatory internship. You will be learning 19 subjects in 4.5 years of your college. The subjects are –  Anatomy Physiology Biochemistry Pathology Microbiology Pharmacology Forensic Medicine & Toxicology Ophthalmology Ear, Nose & Throat (ENT) or Otorhinolaryngology Preventive & Social Medicine Medicine Surgery Obstetrics & Gynecology Pediatrics Psychiatry Dermatology Orthopedics Radiology Anesthesia  Along with these major subjects, there will be minor subdivisions within your subjects like Embryology, Histology, Neuroanatomy, and Parasitology.  We hope we haven’t scared you. This looks like a lot but you will eventually get a hang of it. Let’s break some more misconceptions –  A lotttt to study!!  This is a very popular opinion that in medical school everyone is submerged in books and we are aware our list of subjects above isn’t helping our cause. We won’t lie to you. It’s true but it’s manageable. There are people who have survived medical school before you and you definitely won’t be the last. Toss that worry out the window.  No social life?!  This is an extrapolation of the previous point. Studying doesn’t mean you have to put a stop to your social activities. Medical school is all about learning how to juggle your responsibilities.  You have to mug everything up!  DO NOT DO THIS! We can not stress enough how wrong and misguided this piece of information is. Medicine is nothing to mug up. You need to understand what you are learning and apply them in your practice. Mugging never helps you when a patient comes to you for treatment.  NEET PG preparation must start from your first day!  Absolutely not! Your medical school is for you to learn medicine. Though there is no perfect time for you to start your NEET PG classes/ preparation, you have to navigate your way through medical school.   You have to decide on a specialization in your first year!  No! Medical school is for you to explore all fields and acquire an in-depth knowledge of them. Do not go with a blinkered mindset. Our glorified version of domains might not be the reality. You might lose on golden opportunities to learn in other fields. Theoretical and practical interest is different in medicine. You probably will understand this better once you are in your internship. Some pearls of wisdom for you:  Read daily, do not skip. Make YOUR notes and revise them.  Reference books are THE greatest source of medical knowledge but do not rush towards them just because everyone else is. Find books that you are comfortable with and that you do understand. Do not miss your practicals. Develop your examination and soft skills. Do not undervalue your minor subjects like Embryology, Histology, and Neuroanatomy in the first year. Make use of YouTube and the vast knowledge that it provides. Medical school can be and will be brutal. You could give your best and still not get the desired results but be patient. What doesn’t kill you only makes you stronger! Pursue your hobbies. Find time for yourself. Medical school gets overwhelming, and we understand that, but this is your first major college experience, and make the most of it.  All the best!

blog_title: JoSAA 2022 Counseling FAQs | Know the Answers to Most Common JoSAA Counseling Queries
description: JoSAA registration process has commenced now and the display of the first mock seat allocation will be on the 18th of September, Sunday. With the ongoing process, you must be having some queries about it. This post will help you and our future aspirants clear all of their doubts.  WHAT IS JoSAA?  The Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) conducts the admission process for engineering colleges like IITs, NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs. It admits students via JEE Main and JEE Advanced marks. Click here to know more about JoSAA 2022 schedule. JoSAA 2022 will be admitting students via JEE Main 2022 and JEE Advanced 2022 results. Stay tuned to know about your prospective college based on your JEE Advanced 2022 and JEE Main 2022 rank with the help of our college predictor.  WHEN WILL JoSAA 2022 COMMENCE?  Registration for JoSAA 2022 has started. It starts after the declaration of IIT Advanced results. Click here to know the complete schedule for JoSAA 2022.  DO I HAVE TO REGISTER FOR JoSAA? CAN’T I APPLY THROUGH ANOTHER PORTAL?  If you want to apply to IITs, NITs, IIITs, or GFTIs then no, you can not apply through via anything else. JoSAA is solely responsible for admissions to these institutions. Apart from JoSAA, you can apply to individual state counseling rounds like MH DTE for Maharashtra, DTE MP for Madhya Pradesh, TNEA for Tamil Nadu, AP EAMCET for Andhra Pradesh, etc. The details for these could be accessed from their respective websites.  DO I HAVE TO PAY FOR JoSAA 2022 REGISTRATION PROCESS?  No, you don’t have to pay any fees for the JoSAA counseling process.  HOW ARE THE SEATS ALLOCATED?  On the basis of JEE Advanced 2022 score and rank, IIT seats are allocated. For NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs, your JEE Main 2022 score and rank are taken into consideration.  CAN I EDIT MY CHOICES AFTER LOCKING THEM?  Yes, you can ONLY before the choice filling deadline. This means you can change your order preference or add more courses or delete some courses. Once the date has passed you cannot make any changes to it. Refer to www.josaa.nic.in for detailed guidelines about this.  I AM UNHAPPY WITH MY ALLOCATED SEAT. I WANT TO WAIT FOR THE NEXT ROUND’S RESULT. HOW DO I GO ABOUT THIS PROCESS?  You can wait for the next round’s result to get your desired college but to be applicable for that process you first need to accept your current seat, upload the required documents and pay the seat acceptance fee. If you fail to do any of the above steps, your seat will be canceled. To be considered for the next round, you need to choose the float/ slide option while accepting a seat in the current round.  WHAT IS FLOAT/ SLIDE?  Float: If you want to participate in the subsequent rounds to upgrade your seat while keeping your allocated seat, you should opt for this option. Slide: If you want to upgrade to a different course within your allocated institute, this is your option.  I AM SATISFIED WITH MY SEAT. WHAT DO I HAVE TO DO NOW?  Freeze: If you are happy with your allocated seat and do not want to take part in the further counseling process, then you could go for this option. Note: Once you have chosen the Freeze option while accepting the seat, you can change to the Float/ Slide option afterward.   I MISSED ONE OF THE STEPS OF THE JoSAA COUNSELING PROCESS. WHAT WILL HAPPEN NOW?  Failure in accepting the seat or uploading the required documents or payment of seat acceptance fees will result in the cancellation of your allocated seat.  I GOT UPGRADED DURING ONE OF THE ROUNDS. NOW, I WANT TO GO BACK TO MY PREVIOUS SEAT. HOW DO I GET IT BACK?  You cannot. Once you have been upgraded and accepted a higher seat, your previous seat gets forfeited.  Keep referring to the JoSAA website for new updates. Here is a detailed FAQ report. All the best!
